historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 43, Cable Car Barn and Power House.

Built in 1885–87 for the Powell Street Railway's cars and cable machinery, near the original spring and reservoir of the Spring Valley Water Company; the railway merged into the Ferries and Cliff House Railway in 1887, whose name and that year are on both street fronts, and the line passed to the Municipal Railway in 1944.

Most of the original three-storey building burned in the 1906 fire; it was rebuilt with two storeys to much the same appearance, and the cable engines, steam-driven until then, were converted to electric motors.
